reviewed_by: Claude, with kernel tests against a disposable root runner and a fake staging Core replay
reason: Host commands now run inside a protected local memory runner (nebula.memory-runner/v1): a root service that creates a root-owned cgroup-v2 group per Host worker job, verifies limits by kernel readback, starts each command inside it with no capabilities, no_new_privs, cleared groups and hidden daemon sockets, and proves cleanup with cgroup.kill plus group removal. The selection covers host job admission, OOM settlement, lost-create and unverified-cleanup handling, dead-owner reconciliation with runner authority checks, running-limit readback, the held path without a runner, the memory budgets API (local capability), supervisor memory control, and the DEB mapping for the runner and its unit.
exclusions: Not run in CI: the two kernel tests in test_host_memory_runner.py (they need NEBULA_TEST_HOST_MEMORY_RUNNER_SOCKET pointing at a root runner; run locally against nebula-memory-runner@agent and passing), PostgreSQL parametrizations, the full suite, and the browser. Excluded because they fail identically on origin/main: test_runtime_memory_control.py::test_saved_floor_policy_is_repaired_through_host_before_api_admission (reserve floor) and test_packaging.py::test_nebula3_runtime_has_no_conditional_import_fallbacks (five pre-existing modules; this branch adds none). tests/v3/test_automation_runtime.py is excluded: 9 Host-mode tests fail on main because of the memory hold; with a runner present 6 of them now pass, and the other 3 fail for unrelated pre-existing reasons (consent policy, Kali runtime, scope bypass default).
